question.text: As per SEBI's October 2024 clarification on foreign investment in AIFs with Sponsor/Manager from land-border-sharing countries, which condition applies for downstream investment by an AIF to be considered 'domestic' (not indirect foreign investment)?

answer.text: At least 75% of LPs must be Indian residents
The AIF corpus must be entirely INR-denominated
The fund must be listed on a recognised Indian stock exchange
If Sponsor/Manager are individuals, they must be resident Indian citizens; if entities, they must be Indian-owned AND Indian-controlled, ensuring 'control' of the AIF is with Sponsor/Manager

explanation.text: The Logic: Per RBI Notification FEMA 355/2015-RB and subsequent clarifications: downstream investment by an AIF is treated as INDIRECT FOREIGN INVESTMENT if the Sponsor/Manager/Investment Manager is not Indian-owned AND Indian-controlled. The RBI notification permits treating downstream investments as DOMESTIC if 'Control' of the fund is with the Sponsor/Manager (with general exclusion of others). If Sponsor/Manager are individuals, they must be RESIDENT INDIAN CITIZENS. The extent of foreign investment in the corpus is NOT a factor — only Sponsor/Manager ownership and control matters. The Trap: Option A uses a 75% LP threshold — wrong; the corpus composition doesn't matter, only Sponsor/Manager control does. Option B is irrelevant (INR denomination). Option C confuses with listing optionality. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this identically. Cross-references with FEMA NDI Rules Rule 6 (land-border restriction for China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar). SEBI Oct 8, 2024 Circular codifies the 50%-of-corpus diligence trigger for land-border investors. Manager's Pro-Tip: If your fund has 30%+ foreign LPs, structure the Sponsor/Manager as Indian-owned-and-controlled (≥51% Indian shareholding + majority Indian directors + no foreign veto) to preserve the domestic-downstream treatment. Document this in a 'Control Chart' annexure to Form A.
